idiom_name: Play ActionFunction/ActionRefiner pipeline composed with andThen (PermissionCheckAction)
implementation_notes: Play models the pattern as a stack of action functions: an ActionBuilder provides the entry point, ActionTransformer/ActionRefiner add context (the authenticated user, the loaded item) and an ActionFilter refuses the request with Forbidden, all composed with andThen - the framework's own example ends the chain with a PermissionCheckAction. Because composition happens before (or, with deferred body parsing, independently of) body parsing, a denied request is rejected early and never reaches the controller. In http4s/ZIO HTTP the same seam is middleware wrapping HttpRoutes (AuthedRoutes for the authenticated variant); either way the decision stays in one place and every route is built through the guarded builder.
pitfalls: An action not built through the guarded ActionBuilder (a plain Action, or a controller method bypassing the chain) has no check at all: the routes must use the custom builder everywhere.
Future-based filters that swallow failures (returning None on an error path, or a blocking DAO call inside the filter) let the chain continue instead of denying.
The filter reading identity from the session can see a stale principal after logout; take the subject from the request the guard built rather than re-reading mutable state.
